where: READING CHECK: "BISCUIT" AND "THE REEDS OF THE NORTH LAGOON" A q13
answer: Kiran changes from trying too hard and feeling rejected to being patient and quiet, and that is how he wins Biscuit's trust. At the beginning, Kiran thinks Biscuit wants nothing to do with him; she hides when he talks to her and tries to coax her out [3, 4]. Mrs. Abara's notes said 'Biscuit hides when people talk, so keep quiet around her' [1], but Kiran keeps calling her anyway. By the end, when Biscuit comes out, Kiran stops in the middle of a sentence because he worries that talking will make her hide again [7]. This shows he has learned to be quiet and patient and to think about what Biscuit needs instead of what he wants. He changes from frustrated and pushy to calm and understanding.
note: The story type's default arc (a discouraged, pushy sitter learns patience), built from q1, q3, q4 C and q5. Paragraph numbers come from q4's brackets.
